content.text:
View A: The model represents a yellow circle at the lower location, a blue square at upper, a green triangle at right, and an uncommitted (flat) object at left. Attention is almost entirely on the lower (yellow circle); the other three locations are barely selected and have low immediate availability. Recoverability for the lower object is substantially higher than for the others; the left object is the least recoverable. Predicted effects of commands show the system strongly persisting on the currently targeted location: commands mostly keep selection where it already is, so the modelled allocation in view A is largely resistant to redirection.

View B: The model represents a blue triangle at lower, a red square at upper, a green cross at left, and a yellow circle at right. Attention is almost entirely on the lower (blue triangle); upper and left are available to some degree, right is minimally selected. Recoverability for the lower object is highest. Command predictions concentrate future selection on the right location for many commands, so directing attention in view B tends to shift or lock selection toward the right location rather than freely to every alternative.
